boundary: Fresh official Chromium 141.0.7390.37 revision 1194 was spawned with the native harness exact headless/debugging/extension arguments, fresh owned profile, and unchanged 5000 ms readiness limit. It created SingletonLock and Local State but never DevToolsActivePort. Child remained alive, so spawn/executable permission and immediate crash are excluded. CDP owner verification and product acceptance were never reached.
comparison: Fresh revision 1194 bundle is byte-identical to cached revision 1194. A separate installed Chromium 1228 app bundle shows the same read-only codesign “code has no resources but signature indicates they must be present” diagnostic and ad hoc/no-sealed-resources metadata. This makes the codesign diagnostic non-discriminating; 1228 was not launched.

ranked_hypotheses.cause: Chromium startup blocks in an OS service or framework before CDP initialization
ranked_hypotheses.prediction: A stack sample during the next bounded launch will show its main thread waiting in a specific OS call; unified logs may identify that service.
An otherwise identical bounded launch without extension switches reaches DevToolsActivePort while the full launch does not.

ranked_hypotheses.cause: External-volume file or profile I/O stalls startup
ranked_hypotheses.prediction: A same-revision bounded launch with executable and profile on internal storage reaches the endpoint; process sample shows filesystem wait in this run.

ranked_hypotheses.cause: Readiness limit expires during ordinary cold startup
ranked_hypotheses.prediction: A monitored launch with the unchanged limit fails at five seconds but a separately observed endpoint appears later without a process/argument change; this must not be used to silently raise the limit.

next_discriminating_probe: Two diagnostic launches consumed. Escalate with the sanitized stack evidence to the owner; no third launch, Keychain entry mutation, security-setting change, password-store bypass, signature/quarantine change, endpoint-timeout increase, or acceptance retry in this lane.
scope: Two owned guarded diagnostic launches only; no product file changed, app built, user browser/profile reused, Keychain modified, security setting changed, or acceptance case run. Both resource permits ended valid.

second_probe.launch: Same fresh official Chromium and native harness arguments; new isolated owned profile; unchanged five-second readiness limit; no acceptance or credentials.
second_probe.main_thread_stack: One-second sample near 3.6–4.6 seconds: 703/703 samples follow Chromium main thread → SecItemCopyMatching → SecKeychainItemCopyContent → SecurityServer::ClientSession::decrypt → mach_msg2_trap. This is a synchronous macOS Keychain decrypt wait before CDP endpoint creation.
second_probe.process_cleanup: Chromium parent and both observed helpers absent after owned cleanup; parent required SIGKILL after SIGTERM did not complete within one second.
second_probe.limits: Stack sample identifies the immediate blocking call, not the keychain item, permission-dialog state, securityd cause, or whether the same wait occurs on another host. No raw sample or profile data committed.

verdict: The local native endpoint timeout is caused immediately by Chromium main-thread waiting synchronously for macOS Keychain decryption before DevToolsActivePort creation. The item and reason for the wait remain unknown. Byte-identical official browser content and identical codesign diagnostics exclude cached-binary damage as an explanation.
